level: versioned container-command Task backend: Agent container_command_v1 plus the Host remote-command backend, journal, contract and machine gating
componentAcceptance: verified end to end with real Docker containers on the Ubuntu fixture; dispatch, dedup, unknown-outcome, bounded cancel-with-receipt and alias refusal all pass
productAcceptance: partial; product Task/UI registration stays gated per the design's gate 5, and Windows remains a separate OS-boundary task
implementation: Agent: container_command_v1 is a distinct mutating catalog tool. A non-container Agent settles the operation as never-started (notStarted/stopConfirmed/possiblyApplied:false, CONTAINER_COMMAND_UNAVAILABLE) instead of throwing — a thrown refusal would strand an unsettled admitted operation and an unknown Task forever — and there is no native fallback anywhere in the chain; argv is the only input shape. Container admission lists the tool for physical-root exclusion.

Host contract: parseRemoteTaskCommand accepts only bound machine/root, a bounded workspace-relative directory (empty = root), a 1..64 argv of bounded non-secret strings and a 1000..600000ms deadline; script, env, endpoint, cwd and every extra field are refused.

Host backend: createRemoteCommandBackend mirrors the remote-file discipline — target descriptor with machine/binding revisions, journal checkpoint before dispatch, bounded polling, receipt validation against the original operation identity and strict supervisor stop evidence (never a terminal status alone), dropped-reply unknown with lock retention and observation-only reconciliation, and dispatch-not-sent settled as never-started. Cancellation requests the original cancel, then observes the original operation to terminal within a bounded window that tolerates a real docker teardown; anything less settles unknown.

task-service accepts the scoped-remote-command-v1 write contract; task-journal's execution-reference validation maps remote-write→fs_write and remote-command→container_command_v1; remote-machines gains the tool with per-backend mutating-tool grant checks in taskTarget.

platforms.platform: Ubuntu 24.04 / Node v22.22.1 / linux 6.8.0-101-generic / real Docker / pinned node image
platforms.scope: existing verified fixture with DSH_TEST_DOCKER=1; the container workspace carries the E71 operator grant (the fixture prepares only its own tree)
platforms.combined: 21/21 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped (remote-command 7 with real containers, remote-write-tasks 14 unchanged)
21 tests, 16 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped (the five Docker-gated dispatch cases are explicit skips; the contract and non-container refusal cases run for real), exit 0

platforms.rootRegression: 1828 tests, 1765 pass, 0 fail, 63 skipped, exit 0 (log: tmp/integration/command-facade-root-regression-final.log); the suite is registered in npm test and Windows/Ubuntu CI

preservedFailures: The first Ubuntu run failed 5 dispatch cases: the admission journal rejected the new tool (WORKSPACE_TOOL_NOT_SUPPORTED — the tool list is now explicit), and three test-side issues were found with real containers (success/possiblyApplied semantics, a racy lock assertion, a missing task-level cancel call) plus a 5s cancel window that real docker teardown exceeds and a 0700 fixture workspace that the 65532 worker cannot write — the last is exactly the E71 operator-grant contract, so the fixture now prepares its own permissions. Each was fixed and rerun to green; none were silenced.
limitations: Product Task/UI registration (design gate 5), the strict-model shell gating review and the Windows OS-boundary command path remain open; this checkpoint does not open model-facing command tools.

argv aliases resolve through the container configuration's owner-approved executables only; no endpoint, environment, credential or arbitrary host executable is reachable, and worktree/Git stays refused in container mode.

The bounded cancel-observation window (20s) settling unknown on expiry is conservative by design; a torn-down container beyond the window needs observation-based reconciliation like any other unknown.
Real model inference, billing integration and user-workspace migration remain separate acceptance work.
